name: Deleting Numbers
description: This is an interactive problem. There is an unknown integer $$$x$$$ ($$$1\le x\le n$$$). You want to find $$$x$$$. At first, you have a set of integers $$$\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$$$. You can perform the following operations no more than $$$10000$$$ times: A $$$a$$$: find how many numbers are multiples of $$$a$$$ in the current set. B $$$a$$$: find how many numbers are multiples of $$$a$$$ in this set, and then delete all multiples of $$$a$$$, but $$$x$$$ will never be deleted (even if it is a multiple of $$$a$$$). In this operation, $$$a$$$ must be greater than $$$1$$$. C $$$a$$$: it means that you know that $$$x=a$$$. This operation can be only performed once. Remember that in the operation of type B $$$a \gt 1$$$ must hold. Write a program, that will find the value of $$$x$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1\le n\le 10^5$$$). The remaining parts of the input will be given throughout the interaction process.
approach_summary: Design an adaptive query strategy maintaining uncertainty bounds. Halve candidate space or probe tree centroids using at most the allowed query budget.
